subject.title: Feature request: Escalating stall recovery for sub-agents (nudge → kill)

question: Should OpenClaw add default-on two-stage subagent inactivity recovery, and what activity signal, thresholds, nudge content, kill semantics, parent wake contract, and channel-visible notification behavior should it use?
rationale: The remaining work adds public config/default behavior, mutating child-run recovery, session queue unblocking, and user-visible channel semantics, so automation cannot safely choose the policy from source evidence alone.

options.title: Define core recovery policy
options.body: Maintainers specify the default or opt-in stance, activity source, nudge and kill semantics, parent wake behavior, and channel notification contract before implementation.

options.title: Prototype default-off watchdog
options.body: Allow an experimental opt-in implementation first, with focused live proof and no behavior change for existing installs until maintainers accept defaults.

options.title: Defer automatic recovery
options.body: Rely on runTimeoutSeconds, diagnostics recovery, and future manual kill/reap controls until more production evidence or policy direction exists.

recommendation.title: Define core recovery policy
recommendation.body: Maintainers specify the default or opt-in stance, activity source, nudge and kill semantics, parent wake behavior, and channel notification contract before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: This account has the strongest recent history across subagent control, registry, and orchestration boundaries that this product decision would extend.
